name: Bilgah
overview: Bilgah was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, explicitly identified as a descendant of Aaron. He is noted in Scripture as one of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel, playing a role in the restoration period after the exile. His priestly lineage underscores his service in the religious leadership of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Bilgah means "gleam" or "smile," reflecting a proper name without direct divine origin. This name is recorded in Nehemiah 12:5 and does not carry additional titles beyond his priestly designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Bilgah was a descendant of Aaron, situating him within the priestly family line. No other family relationships are documented beyond this priestly heritage.
scriptureSignificance: Bilgah's significance lies in his role as a priest who returned with Zerubbabel, contributing to the reestablishment of worship and religious order in Jerusalem after the exile. As a descendant of Aaron, he represents the continuation of the Levitical priesthood during a critical period of restoration. His mention in Nehemiah highlights the importance of faithful priestly leadership in the rebuilding of the community and temple worship.
